question: How do I register for courses each semester?
answer: Course registration opens on the student portal about two weeks before each semester starts. Log in with your student ID, open the Registration page, and pick the courses listed for your department and year. Check that the course times do not overlap, confirm your choices, and print the confirmation page. Your advisor must approve the registration before the deadline, so visit them early if you have questions about prerequisites.

question: How can I add or drop a course after the semester starts?
answer: You can add or drop a course during the first two weeks of the semester using the add/drop form from the registrar's office.   Get your advisor's signature first, then submit the form. After the deadline a dropped course appears on your record with a W grade.

question: What is the maximum number of credit hours I can take?
answer: Most students may take up to 21 credit hours in one semester. Students with a cumulative GPA above 3.5 can ask the department head for permission to take extra credit hours.

question: How do I borrow books from the library?
answer: Bring your student ID to the circulation desk. You can borrow up to five books for two weeks and renew them once online if nobody else has reserved them. Late books are charged a small fine per day.

question: Can I access digital journals from my dorm?
answer: Yes. The library subscribes to several online journal databases. Log in to the library website with your student account and you can read and download articles from your dorm or from home. If a journal asks for a separate password, contact the library help desk.

question: What are the library opening hours?
answer: The library is open from 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM on weekdays and from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays and public holidays, except during exam weeks when it stays open late.

question: How do I connect to the campus Wi-Fi?
answer: Choose the network called CampusNet from your Wi-Fi list and sign in with your student portal username and password. If the sign-in page does not open, forget the network, reconnect, and open any website in your browser. Wi-Fi is strongest in the library, the main lecture halls and the computer labs.

question: I forgot my student portal password. What should I do?
answer: Click Forgot password on the portal login page and follow the steps sent to your university email. If you no longer have access to that email, visit the IT help desk in the main building with your student ID and they will reset it for you.

question: Where can I get free software like Office or MATLAB?
answer: Students can download Microsoft Office and several engineering tools for free using their university email address. Open the software page on the IT website, sign in, and follow the installation guide for your computer. Licences stay valid as long as you are an enrolled student.

question: How do I apply for a make-up exam?
answer: If you missed an exam for a serious reason such as illness or a family emergency, submit a make-up exam request to your department within three working days. Attach proof, for example a medical certificate. The department will tell you the new date by email.

question: How can I request a re-check of my exam grade?
answer: Fill in the grade review form at the registrar's office within one week after the results are published. Pay the small review fee, and your paper will be re-marked by a different instructor. The new grade replaces the old one even if it is lower.

question: What items are allowed in the exam hall?
answer: You may bring your student ID, pens, pencils and an approved calculator. Phones, smart watches, notes and bags must be left at the front of the hall. Anyone caught with unauthorised material can be reported for academic misconduct.

question: How do I apply for a dormitory room?
answer: Dormitory applications open on the student affairs page one month before the semester starts. Fill in the online form, upload a copy of your ID, and wait for the allocation list. First-year students and students living far from campus get priority.

question: Can I change my dorm room or roommate?
answer: Room changes are possible during the first month of the semester. Ask the dormitory office for a room change form, explain the reason, and wait for approval. Changes depend on empty beds.

question: How do I pay tuition and where can I get a receipt?
answer: Tuition can be paid at any partner bank branch or through mobile banking using your student ID as the payment reference. Bring the bank slip to the finance office, where you will receive an official receipt. Keep the receipt because you may need it for scholarship or visa paperwork.

question: Are scholarships available and how do I apply?
answer: Yes. The university offers merit scholarships for students with high grades and need-based support for students from low-income families. Applications open every year in the first month of the semester. You need your latest transcript, a short personal statement and a recommendation letter from an instructor.

question: What happens if I miss the tuition payment deadline?
answer: Late payments are charged a late fee for every week after the deadline. If you cannot pay on time because of a real hardship, write to the finance office before the deadline to ask for a payment plan.

question: How do I join or start a student club?
answer: Visit the student affairs office or the club fair at the start of each semester to join an existing club. To start a new club you need at least ten interested students, a faculty advisor and a short proposal describing the club's activities.

question: Where can I find information about hackathons and coding competitions?
answer: The computing departments and the coding clubs announce hackathons on the notice boards and in the department Telegram groups. Many events let beginners join in teams, so you do not need to be an expert. Ask your department's club leader to add you to the announcement group.

question: Is there a clinic on campus and is it free?
answer: The campus clinic is open every weekday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Consultations are free for registered students, and basic medicines are provided at a reduced price. For emergencies outside opening hours, go to the nearest hospital and bring your student ID.

question: Who can I talk to if I feel stressed or overwhelmed?
answer: The student counselling office offers free and confidential appointments. You can book a time at the desk in the student affairs building or ask a lecturer to refer you. Talking early about stress, anxiety before exams or personal problems helps a lot.

question: How do I find internships?
answer: The career office posts internship openings on its notice board and website every semester and invites companies for career days. You can also ask your department head for company contacts. Prepare your CV and a short cover letter before you apply.

question: Can the university help me prepare my CV?
answer: Yes. The career office runs short CV and interview workshops during the semester, and you can book a one-to-one review of your CV for free.

question: Is there a shuttle between the campus and the city?
answer: University buses run between the campus main gate and the city centre every morning and evening on weekdays. The timetable is posted at the main gate and on the student affairs page. Students show their ID card to board.

question: How do I get an official transcript?
answer: Request it at the registrar's office with your student ID and pay the transcript fee. Normal processing takes three working days. Sealed copies for other universities or employers can be sent directly if you give the address.
